messages:
micah: heads-up — planning a synthetic load run to validate admission/backpressure thresholds across regions tomorrow 03:00 UTC. goal: confirm queueing + graceful fallback between hosted and dedicated pools. volunteers? :rocket:
anya: I can own the runbook and the test harness. which thresholds do we want to validate? 75/85/95% GPU util or queue-length limits?
devon: prioritize these KPIs: P50/P95 latency, request_queue_depth, admission_reject_count, gpu_utilization, kv_cache_evictions. also capture cost delta + pod churn.
lina: noted. I'll draft Grafana panels and a short alert set. will also watch per-region capacity (us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast).
micah: test profile: ramp 0->1k rps over 10m, hold 15m, spike to 2k for 5m, then cool-down. run against g5 and p2 pools and a dedicated small pool. run three passes with admission thresholds at 75,85,95. capture full traces.
infra-bot: action: scheduled synthetic-run sl-run-1783001123 by micah at 2027-05-12T03:00:00Z. runner: loadgen-v2. status: queued.
anya: load generator command to use (for reproducibility):
```bash
# run from infra CI runner
rb-loadgen \
  --targets=redwood-prod-us-west,redwood-prod-eu-west,redwood-prod-ap-southeast \
  --gpu-pools=g5,p2,dedicated-small \
  --profile=ramp-hold-spike \
  --ramp=600 --hold=900 --spike-duration=300 --rps=1000,2000 \
  --kv-cache=enabled --emit-prometheus=127.0.0.1:9091 \
  --metadata=job=backpressure-validation,pass=${PASS} \
  --report=/tmp/loadgen-${PASS}.json
```
micah: question: should we enable request-level retries on the client side for this? would obscure admission rejects. probably disable retries for first passes.
lina: agree — disable retries and circuit-breakers so we see raw admission behavior. :eyes: 
devon: quick cost estimate: running full sweep across 3 regions + 2 GPU types for ~40m each -> ~12 instance-hours of high-end GPUs. cost-ops: expect ~$1.5k gross for the run.
cost-ops: confirmed rough ballpark, add buffer for failed retries and extra passes. fine for validation window.
micah: infra note — watch network path to eu-west; last month we saw sporadic packet drops during high fan-out synthetic tests. drop + retry spikes can mask admission controller effects.
sre-oncall: we'll have oncall watching NVMe/cgroup throttles and node network RX/TX. I can flip on detailed qdisc stats for the period.
infra-bot: run-starting: sl-run-1783001123 pass=1 threshold=75% at 2027-05-12T03:00:00Z. job pid=34219.
# (10m later)
infra-bot: metrics snapshot: us-west gpu_util=78% p95=312ms queue_depth=420 admission_throttle_rate=0.03 rps=980
micah: initial pass shows admission kicking in near expected threshold. interesting: queue_depth climbs before throttle count spikes. implies admission window is slightly delayed.
devon: paste of controller log around throttles:
```
[2027-05-12T03:12:23Z] admission_controller INFO allow_rate=950 threshold_util=0.75 gpu_util=0.79 queue_len=360 throttled=82
[2027-05-12T03:12:24Z] admission_controller WARN fallback_to_dedicated=true routed=18
[2027-05-12T03:12:24Z] kvcache DEBUG cache_hits=91% cache_evictions=4
```
lina: noticed eu-west had higher queue depth at lower GPU util: suspected network egress bottleneck. devon, can you check per-node egress bytes/sec?
devon: yep — eu-west node-12 egress peaked at 9.2Gbps and started dropping packets. flows were fan-out to shared redis for kv cache warmup.
micah: action items: 1) add a fast-path network check to harness (iperf-lite) before run, 2) instrument admission controller to emit queue_delay metric sooner, 3) re-run pass at 85% with retries still off.
infra-bot: run-failed: sl-run-1783001123 pass=1 reason=network-degradation eu-west. status=aborted at 2027-05-12T03:18:42Z.
anya: copying runbook snippet into thread: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/backpressure-validation — includes pre-checks, dashboards, and rollback steps.
micah: thanks. pushing the precheck change to loadgen and will requeue. aim to keep total timeboxed to 2h.
lina: also propose we validate a conservative threshold (70%) for eu-west given regional NIC limits. document it in the run results.
devon: for troubleshooting, here's a minimal admission config patch to test quicker windowing:
```yaml
admission:
  window_ms: 500
  sample_interval_ms: 100
  thresholds:
    - name: low
      util: 0.75
    - name: medium
      util: 0.85
    - name: high
      util: 0.95
```
micah: perfect. I'll kick pass=2 at 03:45 UTC after infra prechecks. who'll be watching cost and churn?
cost-ops: I'm on it. will annotate billing and report incremental cost per pass.
sre-oncall: I'll stay pinned during the window and own paging if NVMe/network node errors crop up.
anya: thanks all. will post a short summary in #eng-infra after final pass with screenshots and Prometheus links. :white_check_mark:
